LESSON GOALS
•	 To understand simple stories and conversations.
•	 To ask and answer questions about familiar topics 
(personal information, clothes, colours, weather, etc.).
•	 To understand and talk about dates and numbers.
•	 To describe people’s appearance.

3.– WORKSHEET: LISTEN AND DRAW (P.5) (9’)
Listen and Draw
5
P.3.2
Jason
MATERIALS
•	 Colouring pencils or crayons
NOTE: if you collected your Ss books during the booklet 
activity, have them ask you for it now by saying, “Can I have 
my book please?”; otherwise, ask them to take it out of their 
bag. Explain the activity before giving out the books/asking Ss 
to take them out since they might get distracted.
This worksheet shows a blank outline of a person. Students 
must listen and draw in the details according to your description. 
Make sure that each S has a variety of coloured pencils or crayons. 
Before giving out the books, review the vocabulary needed 
to describe one of the characters from the Activity 2 (P.3.2). For 
example, show the card with Jason on it and say, “Jason has 
got short curly* blonde hair, small green eyes, small ears, a 
big nose and a big mouth. He’s wearing a blue jumper, a pair 
of green shorts and a pair of green shoes.” 
After reviewing the vocabulary, give out the books and invent 
a character description (you can also come up with a name or 
ask your Ss to do so). Describe the character using the structure 
in the previous example. Pause between every physical trait 
so Ss have time to draw. You can set a time limit for each of 
the characteristics.
> For Advanced Students
If your Ss find it too easy, encourage them to take it in turns 
to ask you questions about the character instead of you giving 
the information, for example, “What does her hair look like?” 
or “What does her nose look like, is it big or small?” or “What 
is she wearing?”, etc.

> Scenario A
If your group has achieved the activity goal on My Way (i.e., 
they have done all or most of the activities in the current Mission), 
say, “You’re doing amazing on My Way! You have played lots 
of games in Mission 3, so we can do a special sticker activity 
together!”. Take the Day 3 stickers and have them ask, “Can I 
have some stickers, please?”. Do the activity as instructed below. 
> Scenario B
If your group hasn’t reached the activity goal on My Way, 
simply move on with the class. You will have to complete one 
or two activities from the bonus section to make up for the 
time allotted to this dynamic. 
The point of this activity is to review talking about age in a fun 
way. Ss have to stick the stickers and answer the questions by 
looking at the colour combinations. Model the task by looking 
for the stickers, sticking them, and answering the questions.
Have Ss open pp.14-15 (sticker section) and say, “Let’s find 
out how old these people are!”. Point to rectangle number 
one and ask, “What number is this?”. Ss should respond, “It’s

number 1!”. Say, “Can you find number 1 on the sticker sheet? 
Who is it?”, and elicit, “Here it is! It’s Dave.”. Then say, “Look, 
Dave’s age is purple plus pink. That’s 20 + 25!” (point to the 
corresponding circles) “How old is he?”. Help the Ss add up 
the numbers and have them reply, “He’s 45 years old!”
Follow the same procedure for stickers 2-6 and do as many 
as time allows. 
We recommend making this activity more dynamic by turning 
it into a competition to answer the questions as fast as possible. 
You can give points to Ss who respond correctly. 
If you can’t finish the whole activity, tell the Ss that they can 
continue at home.
KEY
Sticker 1 (Dave): How old is he? He is 45 years old. 
Sticker 2 (Matt): How old is he? He is 4 years old.
Sticker 3 (Lana): How old is she? She is 17 years old.
Sticker 4 (Mary): How old is she? She is 80 years old.
Sticker 5 (Nancy): How old is she? She is 34 years old.
Sticker 6 (Kate): How old is she? She is 2 years old.
6.– ACTIVITY 6: INCORRECT DESCRIPTIONS (7’) 
P.3.2
Joe
> How to Play
Choose a Character playing card (P.3.2) and show it to the 
Ss. Then incorrectly describe the person. Ss will have to correct 
you using full sentences.
> Warm-Up
To introduce the structures, start by saying wrong things 
about the Ss in the group. For example, if Jane has got blonde 
hair, say, “Jane has got brown hair. Is that right or wrong?”
Encourage Ss to correct you by saying, “No, that’s wrong. 
She hasn’t got brown hair. Jane has got blonde hair.”

Say two or three wrong statements about your Ss so they 
can practise correcting you.
> Main Activity
Choose a character playing card, show it to the Ss and make 
a mistake when describing the character. You can say, “Hmm, 
I think I’m a bit confused...” to make it more theatrical. The 
Ss must correct you by saying, for example, “No, that’s wrong. 
She hasn’t got blonde hair. She has got red hair.” Ss love to 
correct the teacher, so you can make this activity more fun by 
exaggerating your mistakes and acting surprised or confused 
when they correct you.
> For Advanced Groups
When your Ss get the gist of the activity, and they are familiar 
with the target language, you can let them take on the teacher 
role and incorrectly describe a character.
7.– ACTIVITY 5: CLOTHING DESCRIPTIONS (9’)
P.3.5
Michelle
Charlie
Joe
1A
> How to Play
Each S will get an A or B A5 flash card. The flash cards 
contain the same characters but on flash card B they are not 
wearing their usual clothes. In pairs, Ss will have to guess the 
differences between the two flash cards.
> Warm-Up
Quickly review the clothing vocabulary by describing your 
own clothing and asking about the Ss’ by saying for example, 
“I’m wearing a black jumper, a pair of blue jeans, a pair of 
red socks and a pair of black boots. What about you Jane? 
What are you wearing?”. The S in question should reply, “I’m 
wearing…”
> Main Activity
Say, “Let’s see if the characters on our cards are wearing the 
same clothes!”. Demonstrate the activity to the Ss beforehand, so

they understand what they must do. You can choose a confident 
S to model the activity. Without looking at each other’s cards, 
the Ss must ask each other questions about the characters’ 
clothes to find out if they are wearing the same thing.
Once they get the gist, divide the Ss into pairs and give each S 
a flash card. One S will be A, and the other will be B. Make sure 
to give each pair the same number (for example, 1A and 1B). 
The Ss will ask each other yes/no questions like, “Is Michelle 
wearing a red jumper?”, to which their classmate should answer 
either “Yes, she is,” or “No, she isn’t. She’s wearing a purple 
jumper.”. Move around the room and monitor their conversations.
> Follow-Up
To follow-up, show two A5 flash cards (P.3.5) and ask the Ss, 
for example, “Look at Michelle. Is she wearing a red jumper 
in flash card B?” to which Ss should answer, “No, she isn’t. 
She is wearing a purple jumper.” After this answer, encourage 
Ss to say, “In flash card A, she is wearing a red jumper, but in 
flash card B she is wearing a purple jumper.”
Do not ask more than two follow-up questions.
8.– ACTIVITY 11: NUMBERS (VERSION 2) (5’)
P.E.M.3
55
This game is based on the traditional game Snap!
Mix the Numbers (P.E.M.3.) with the jokers by getting the Ss 
to say, “Mix, mix, mix” and encouraging them to say “Stop!”
Take the whole deck and start turning over the cards and 
putting them in the middle. The Ss should state whatever number 
comes out by saying, for example, “It’s number 62.”. Whenever 
a joker is turned over, they should say, “Snap!”. Try to keep a 
good pace so that the game is more interesting.
The first S to say, “Snap!” gets all the cards in the middle, and 
the next round starts. The game is over when it’s not possible 
to put more cards in the middle. The winner is the S with the 
most cards.

BONUS
ACTIVITY 4: PLAY DETECTIVE
> How to Play
One S is the detective and has to wait outside the classroom 
while another S (the thief) takes the Purse cutout and hides it 
by putting in their pocket or sitting on it. The detective has to 
find out who the thief is by asking questions.

> Main Activity
Introduce the activity by saying, “Let’s see if the detective 
can find the thief!”
Choose a thief, have them hide the purse, and tell the detective 
to come back into the room. Use the structure: “Detective, 
detective, come in!”. The detective should ask questions to 
the group to find out who has the purse.
Before starting the round, the group can say, “What does the 
thief look like?” (they can sing this part). Then the detective 
can start asking yes or no questions such as:
•	 Has the thief got long hair?
•	 Is the thief wearing black shoes?
•	 Is the thief tall or short?
Always insist that the Ss ask and answer questions in full 
sentences and structures. Discourage the Ss from asking 
whether the thief was a boy or a girl unless they really can’t 
figure out who the thief is, because doing so may make guessing 
who the thief is too easy. 
When the detective is ready to guess, they should ask, “John, 
are you the thief?” and the S being accused should respond, 
“Yes, I am.” or “No, I am not.” If the detective accuses somebody 
wrongly, the thief wins; if the detective accuses somebody and 
their guess is correct, then they win.
> Variation
Once Ss are comfortable playing this game, you can bring 
in some props and have the Ss wear different accessories like 
hats and glasses to make it more fun. This way the detective 
can ask a greater variety of questions. 
NOTE: the first few times you play this game, the Ss might 
need your help. Do not hesitate in helping your Ss complete 
some of the sentences or modelling an example and having 
them repeat the sentence after you.
ACTIVITY 1: MAKE A FACE (VERSION 2)
P.3.1

> Main Activity
Tell your Ss, “It’s time to meet a new friend!”. Use Blu-Tack 
to place the A3 sheet on the whiteboard. Ask your Ss, “What 
is this person’s name?”, and have them choose a name for 
the character. You can write it on the A3 using an erasable 
whiteboard marker.
Then dictate to the Ss what the person looks like. Decide 
which part of the face (Face cutouts) each S is responsible for. 
Say, for example, “John, he/she has got short blonde hair,” and 
have John place the cutouts accordingly. Since not all Ss may 
get a turn, make sure to take note of who does what and vary 
it each time you do this activity.
